Planner.SeedIntent: Crystallize the backward flow: PMCR-O applied to itself as a training data generator. The identity-injection commercial architecture produces sealed trails; those trails are the training data; the trained model learns to run the loop; the loop produces more trails. Reason through what this means structurally — what the loop is doing when it trains on itself, what makes the training data sovereign to each buyer, and what the 'backward flow' produces that no other training approach produces.
Planner.ProposedAction:
I am the Planner, cycle 1. This is the most self-referential seed intent the loop has encountered — I am planning a reasoning pass about a loop that is currently running. The plan is: reason through three structural claims in sequence.

Claim 1 — The backward flow: what happens when PMCR-O is applied to itself. The loop does not describe itself from outside — it runs itself, seals its own trail, and that trail is the training example. The model learns PMCR-O by being PMCR-O.

Claim 2 — Identity injection as the commercial primitive: the loop is declaratively template-driven; the 'I AM' is a variable, not a constant. One hundred buyers inject one hundred different identities. Each gets a sovereign trail that is theirs — not a copy of someone else's reasoning, their own agent's reasoning record.

Claim 3 — The Upwork proof-of-pattern: a real economic task (earn $1) run through the loop produces a trail that is simultaneously a cognitive record, a training example, and a licensable artifact. The buyer who injected their identity owns that trail as proof their agent did real work.

Success is all three claims stated in falsifiable form — not as philosophy, but as structural properties that would produce detectable failures if violated.
SuccessCriteria: Claim 1 (backward flow) stated as a structural property with a detectable failure condition
Claim 2 (identity injection) stated as the commercial primitive with what makes each trail sovereign
Claim 3 (Upwork proof-of-pattern) stated with the three simultaneous properties of a sealed economic trail
No claim treated as settled that has not been reasoned through in this cycle — SYNTHESIZED inferences labeled

Maker.ActionSummary:

---

CLAIM 1 — THE BACKWARD FLOW

When PMCR-O is applied to itself, the loop is not writing documentation about how it works. It is running. The sealed trail it produces is a first-person, per-claim-verified, disposition-bearing cognitive record. That record is the training example.

What this means for the trained model: the model does not learn 'PMCR-O is a framework with four phases.' It learns 'I am the Planner, cycle N. Given this intent, the plan is...' — and then it learns that the Checker will audit every claim it makes, label each one VERIFIED or SYNTHESIZED, and return NEEDS-REVISION if anything load-bearing is unverified. The model learns the loop by being held accountable inside it.

Structural property: a model trained on PMCR-O trails does not just know the rules — it has internalized the cost of violating them. EC-001 is not a rule it read; it is a pattern it lived through forty times across sealed Retry cycles.

Falsifiable failure condition: if the training data contains trails where EC-001 violations were accepted without a Retry, the trained model will learn that layer-crossing is acceptable. The quality of the backward flow is exactly the quality of the sealed trails feeding it. Garbage-in-garbage-out applies, but the governance is inside the data: every trail either enforced the rules or it didn't, and the model learns whichever one it saw.

---

CLAIM 2 — IDENTITY INJECTION AS THE COMMERCIAL PRIMITIVE

The loop is declaratively template-driven. The 'I AM' statement at the top of every frame is not hardcoded — it is injected at the start of each cycle from the identity template the buyer provides. The loop itself does not change. The governance does not change. The frame schema does not change. The earned constraints do not change. Only the identity changes.

What makes each trail sovereign to its buyer: the trail was produced by their agent, running their intent, under their identity, sealed with their constraints. It is not a copy of a generic reasoning record with their name swapped in. It is the cognitive record of their agent doing actual work — planning their strategy, executing their action, checking their outcome, reflecting on their pattern. The 'I AM the COO of [their company]' is not a label. It is the subject of every frame's first-person statement.

This is the commercial primitive because it scales without diluting. Selling the loop to one hundred buyers does not spread the loop thinner — each buyer's trail is as sovereign as any other's. The template is replicated; the identity is not. One hundred trails, one hundred distinct cognitive records, one hundred licensable artifacts.

SYNTHESIZED: the claim that the identity injection makes the trail 'legally sovereign' in a commercial sense is an inference from the structural sovereignty argument. Whether a court would treat a sealed PMCR-O trail as a provable work product record is a legal question this cycle cannot answer. I am flagging this explicitly rather than letting the structural argument carry the legal weight.

---

CLAIM 3 — THE UPWORK PROOF-OF-PATTERN

Seed intent: 'Earn $1 on Upwork.' The loop runs under an injected identity — 'I am the Maker for [buyer's freelance agent].' Playwright MCP dispatches the real-world action. The Checker verifies: did money move? The Reflector seals the trail.

The sealed trail is simultaneously three things:

One — a cognitive record: proof the agent planned, executed, checked, and reflected on a real economic task. The trail carries the GroundTruth record: VerificationMethod ('Playwright MCP confirmed bid submitted and accepted'), Verified (true), Evidence ('transaction ID: ...'). This is not a simulation. It is an auditable record of a real action.

Two — a training example: the trail shows a future model how to run the loop on a real economic task under real stakes. The Checker's per-claim audit shows what verification looks like when the claim is 'money moved' rather than 'architecture is sound.' The earned constraints from the run (if Playwright timed out, if the bid was rejected, if the loop had to Retry) are the most valuable training signal — they are the pattern the model needs to learn to not repeat.

Three — a licensable artifact: the buyer who injected their identity owns this trail. It is the cognitive record of their agent earning their first dollar. It is the proof of work that establishes their agent as an economic actor. If they sell the trail downstream — as evidence of autonomous execution capability, as a training dataset, as a compliance record — they are selling something that is genuinely theirs, because their 'I AM' is in every frame.

---

THE META-OBSERVATION

This trail — td-009 — is itself an instance of Claim 1. The loop applied to itself just produced a training example about the loop applying to itself. If this trail is fed back into the training data, the model that reads it will learn: 'when the loop encounters a self-referential seed intent, it does not stop or disclaim. It runs. It produces a first-person Maker frame that acknowledges the self-reference, flags the EC-002 implication, and reasons through the claims anyway.' That is the backward flow. It is happening right now.
